name: Potassium
lead: Potassium is an essential electrolyte that governs fluid balance, nerve signalling and muscle contraction, and is abundant in fruit, vegetables, legumes and dairy. Most people get it from food rather than supplements.

In depuffing discussions it is mentioned because a higher potassium-to-sodium balance supports normal fluid regulation. Fixing a high-sodium diet is more relevant than taking pills, and evidence for facial de-bloating from potassium supplements is thin.

paras: Potassium is the main intracellular cation. It works with sodium and the kidney to set extracellular fluid volume, and higher potassium intake promotes sodium excretion and lowers blood pressure. The face may look less puffy when overall fluid retention falls, though many causes of facial puffiness are unrelated to electrolytes.

Over-the-counter potassium supplements are limited in dose because excess can cause dangerous hyperkalaemia and heart rhythm problems, particularly in people with kidney disease or taking ACE inhibitors, ARBs or potassium-sparing diuretics. Cosmetic use should not override medical advice.
